en: n. food put on a hook or in a trap to catch fish or animals; something used to attract or tempt someone; v. to put food on a hook; to deliberately make someone angry by teasing
ex: The fisherman put a worm on the hook as bait.
漁夫把一條蟲掛在鉤子上當餌。

en: n. the ability to use your knowledge and experience to make good decisions and judgments; knowledge gained over time; a wise saying
ex: With age comes wisdom.
智慧隨年歲而來。

en: a. following the customs or ways of behaving that have been used by a particular group for a long time; of an old or established type
ex: They celebrated the festival in the traditional way.
他們以傳統的方式慶祝這個節日。

en: a. being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else; special or unusual; belonging to or connected with one particular place or person
ex: Every snowflake is unique.
每一片雪花都是獨一無二的。

en: a. not deep; having a small distance from top to bottom; not showing serious thought or real feeling; n. a shallow area of water; v. to become less deep
ex: The children played in the shallow end of the pool.
孩子們在泳池的淺水區玩耍。

en: n. facts or information that show something is true; a test of whether something is good enough; the alcohol content of a drink; a. able to resist something; v. to treat a material to resist water
ex: The police need more proof before they can arrest him.
警方需要更多證據才能逮捕他。

en: n. a narrow street or path between buildings; a long narrow area for playing certain games such as bowling or tennis
ex: A cat ran down the narrow alley behind the restaurant.
一隻貓沿著餐廳後面的窄巷跑過去。

en: a. happy and positive; bright and pleasant; willing and without complaint
ex: She has a cheerful smile that lights up the room.
她有著一個照亮整個房間的開朗笑容。

en: n. a person who owns or has an important position in a bank; a person who runs a gambling game and pays the winners
ex: The banker explained the terms of the loan to us.
銀行家向我們說明了貸款條款。

en: n. a kind of heavy, sticky earth that becomes hard when it is baked, used to make pots and bricks; (literary) the human body
ex: The potter shaped the wet clay into a bowl.
陶匠把濕黏土捏成一個碗。

en: a. unhappy, worried or angry; (of the stomach) feeling sick; v. to make someone unhappy or worried; to knock something over; to change something so that it does not go as planned; n. a surprise result
ex: She was upset because she failed the exam.
她因為考試沒過而心煩。

en: to make someone remember something or think about something; to cause someone to remember something or someone
ex: Please remind me to call him tomorrow.
請提醒我明天打給他。

en: to make it possible for someone to do something; to give someone the ability or the authority to do something; to make something possible
ex: This software enables you to edit photos easily.
這個軟體讓你能輕鬆編輯照片。

en: n. the act of keeping someone or something safe from harm; something that keeps someone or something safe; a system of laws or taxes that protect a country's own industries
ex: Sunscreen offers protection from the sun's harmful rays.
防曬乳可以保護皮膚不受有害紫外線傷害。

en: n. salted or smoked meat from the back or sides of a pig, often cut in thin slices and fried
ex: I had bacon and eggs for breakfast.
我早餐吃了培根和蛋。

en: n. a flat shape with three straight sides and three angles; something shaped like this; a musical instrument made of a metal bar bent in this shape; a situation involving three people
ex: A triangle has three sides and three angles.
三角形有三個邊和三個角。

en: n. a very large reptile that lived millions of years ago; (informal) something very old-fashioned
ex: Children love learning about dinosaurs.
孩子們喜歡了解恐龍。

en: n. (US) a tap that controls the flow of water; a device for controlling the flow of a liquid from a pipe or barrel
ex: Turn off the faucet when you brush your teeth.
刷牙時請關掉水龍頭。

en: n. a particular way of doing something, especially one that needs skill; the skill with which something is done; a method
ex: He learned a new technique for taking better photos.
他學了一個拍出更好照片的新技巧。

en: n. the third month of the year; a walk by a group of people with regular steps, especially soldiers; a long walk; a piece of music with a strong beat; v. to walk with regular steps like a soldier; to move forward with determination; to make someone walk somewhere
ex: Thousands of people marched through the streets to protest.
數千人遊行走過街頭抗議。

en: a. happening or done without delay; closest in relationship, time or place; direct and with nothing in between
ex: The company took immediate action to fix the problem.
公司立即採取行動解決問題。

en: n. a process in which people vote to choose a person for an official position; the fact of being chosen for a job or office; a decision made by choosing from several things
ex: The presidential election will be held next November.
總統大選將於明年十一月舉行。

en: n. a reduction in the usual price of something; v. to reduce the price of something; to consider something to be unimportant or not true; to buy a bill for less than its face value
ex: The shop offers a ten percent discount for students.
這家店提供學生九折優惠。

en: n. a curved piece of wood, metal or plastic with a hook used for hanging clothes; a device on which something hangs
ex: She put her dress on a hanger in the closet.
她把洋裝掛在衣櫥的衣架上。

en: v. to laugh at someone in a friendly or unkind way; to annoy someone on purpose; to comb hair so that it stands up; n. a person who teases
ex: The kids teased her about her new haircut.
孩子們拿她的新髮型開玩笑。

en: n. a sound that is repeated because the sound waves bounce off a surface; the repetition of an idea or opinion; v. to be repeated as a sound bouncing off a surface; to repeat what someone else has said
ex: We heard the echo of our voices in the cave.
我們在山洞裡聽到自己聲音的回音。

en: to tell someone what you think they should do; to officially tell someone about something; to recommend something
ex: The doctor advised him to get more rest.
醫生建議他多休息。

en: a small flying insect that bites people and animals and sucks their blood, sometimes spreading diseases
ex: A mosquito bit me on the arm last night.
昨晚有隻蚊子叮了我的手臂。

en: prep. to a position on a surface; to or on top of something; (informal) aware of or knowing about something; connected to something
ex: The cat jumped onto the table.
貓跳到桌子上。

en: n. a person who does not win a game or competition; a person who fails often or is unsuccessful in life; (informal) a person who is not liked or admired; someone or something that loses something
ex: He doesn't like being the loser of the game.
他不喜歡當遊戲的輸家。

en: n. a cord used to tie shoes; a delicate cloth with a pattern of small holes; v. to tie something with a cord; to add a small amount of alcohol to a drink
ex: Tie your shoelaces so you don't trip.
把鞋帶繫好以免絆倒。

en: n. a set of tools or equipment for a particular purpose; clothes and equipment for a particular activity; a set of parts to make something
ex: Every home should have a first-aid kit.
每個家庭都應該備有急救箱。

en: a. having or showing skill; good at doing something; done with skill and care
ex: She is a skillful pianist with years of training.
她是位接受過多年訓練的技巧純熟的鋼琴家。

en: n. a short stop in an action or speech; a break; v. to stop doing something for a short time; to stop speaking or moving for a moment; n. a button for stopping a video or music
ex: He paused for a moment before answering the question.
他停頓了一下才回答問題。

en: n. an area of houses on the edge of a large town or city; (suburbs) the outer parts of a city
ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
他們住在市區外一個安靜的郊區。

en: v. to drink something slowly in small amounts; n. a small amount of liquid that you drink at one time
ex: She sipped her tea slowly while reading the newspaper.
她一邊看報紙，一邊慢慢啜飲著茶。

en: a. made of wood; stiff or awkward and showing no emotion; (of a voice or face) lacking expression
ex: They sat on a wooden bench in the park.
他們坐在公園的木頭長椅上。

en: a. done, used or situated outside a building; happening in the open air; liking to be in the open air
ex: We have an outdoor swimming pool at the hotel.
我們飯店有一座露天游泳池。

en: n. a small piece of film or video taken from a longer one; a metal or plastic object used to hold things together; v. to fasten something with a clip; to cut small pieces off something; to hit someone lightly
ex: She used a clip to hold her hair back.
她用髮夾把頭髮夾住。

en: n. an agreement to risk money on the result of a race or game; the amount of money that you risk; a guess about what will happen; v. to risk money on something; to think that something is likely to happen
ex: I bet he will be late again tomorrow.
我敢打賭他明天又會遲到。
